items.title: Leadership change coming to Mississauga, Brampton, Caledon schools as province stays in control
items.summary: Parents and students in Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon are facing another leadership change at the Peel District School Board, with Director of Education and CEO Rashmi Swarup preparing to retire at the end of November. Her departure comes during another turbulent chapter for the region’s public school board, which has twice been placed under provincial supervision following concerns about systemic racism, governance problems and financial mismanagement. The retirement also raises questions about who will oversee the board’s day-to-day operations and thousands of employees as the provincial government continues to exercise control over its affairs. The PDSB serves approximately 145,000 students across more than 260 schools and education sites in Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon, making it one of Ontario’s largest school boards. Swarup announced her retirement on June 2, bringing to a close a tenure that began in 2021 when she was appointed to lead the board during its first period of provincial supervision. She was brought in to help turn around an institution facing serious problems after a provincial investigation exposed systemic anti-Black racism, discrimination against students and significant governance failures. Her mandate included implementing 27 binding provincial directives, improving equity and accountability, and rebuilding trust among students, parents, staff and community groups. That provincial supervision ended in 2023, when governance responsibilities were returned to elected trustees.

items.title: Toronto teen wanted in two murders, including killing of young man from Mississauga
items.summary: One of two suspects being hunted by police on Canada-wide arrest warrants in the murder of a young Mississauga man in Toronto is also wanted in connection with another killing three days later, authorities say. Toronto Police said on Monday a 17-year-old Toronto male who’s sought on charges including second-degree murder in the Nov. 7 shooting death of Malik Abass, 18, of Mississauga, is also wanted on a charge of first-degree murder in the Nov. 10 slaying of Brandon Blake, 18, of Barrie. m. on Saturday, Nov. 7. Police officers who responded to the call found him suffering from gunshot wounds. The officers performed life-saving measures on the Mississauga teen before paramedics took him to hospital, where he died a short time later. Suspects fled the scene before police arrived. Malik Abass, 18, of Mississauga, was shot to death in Toronto on Nov. 7. (Photo: Toronto Police) In an update this past Saturday, police said two suspects have been identified in the killing of Abass, Toronto’s 33rd homicide victim of 2026.

items.title: Tinted Windows and a Late Blocking Car Described at Inquest Into 2020 Francique Shooting
items.summary: According to an inquest into the 2020 death of Jamal Francique, Peel police Const. Marc Charlebois testified he was dispatched to a townhouse complex the night a tactical team moved to arrest the 28 year old for an alleged bail violation. Charlebois said he arrived believing there had been an officer involved shooting and a crash, but could not see inside the car because it was dark and the windows were tinted. The inquest heard the officer assigned to block the car in was late, so plainclothes officers on foot and in unmarked vehicles moved to contain it as Francique tried to drive away. One officer on foot fired four shots and a bullet struck Francique in the head, according to an agreed narrative read at the hearing. The car then veered and crashed into a garage pillar, prompting a tactical unit and ambulance to respond, nearly seven years after the Jan. 7, 2020 shooting.

items.title: San Francisco Developer Takes Mississauga to Ontario Land Tribunal Over AI Data Centre Ban
items.summary: According to Global News, San Francisco based developer Prologis has filed with the Ontario Land Tribunal to overturn Mississauga's one year moratorium on artificial intelligence data centres. The company proposed a two storey, 220,000 square foot data centre on former farmland near Tenth Line and Argentia Road, a plan Ward 9 councillor Martin Reid said could include 14 generators and lithium ion batteries, raising noise concerns. Global News reports council voted unanimously to adopt the moratorium, among the first in Canada, after that pushback, and told staff to study the impacts of hosting data centres. Prologis says the direction given to staff was too broad and that the city has not updated it on the study's status. The moratorium took effect in September, and Reid had questioned whether the facility would function more like a power plant, according to the outlet.

items.title: Peel Police Say Driver Stayed at Scene After Mississauga Pedestrian Struck Sunday Night
items.summary: According to Peel Regional Police, a pedestrian was taken to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries after being struck by a vehicle in Mississauga on Sunday evening. Police said on X that officers responded Nov. 15, and a spokesperson told insauga.com on Monday the person's injuries were not life-threatening. Paramedics transported the pedestrian to a local hospital, according to the force. Police did not release the victim's age or gender, and said the driver remained at the scene. The investigation is ongoing, and no charges had been announced as of Monday, police said.

items.title: Peel Police Ask Public to Call 905-453-3311 Over Missing 85-Year-Old Mississauga Man
items.summary: According to Peel Regional Police, officers are searching for an 85 year old man named Noel who was last seen near Queensway East and Hurontario Street around 11 p.m. Sunday. Police describe him as five feet seven inches tall, bald, with a grey and black beard, and say his clothing is unknown since no description was provided. The man's surname was not released by police, who are calling him a vulnerable missing adult. Anyone with information is asked to call 905-453-3311, according to the force. Peel police shared the alert publicly and asked residents to contact them immediately if Noel is spotted.

items.title: Peel's Child Care Fees Have Already Dropped 53 Percent, But $10-a-Day Target Slips to 2027
items.summary: According to Peel Region's 2026-2029 Early Years and Child Care business plan, daily fees across Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon have already fallen about 53 per cent since 2024 and are capped at 22 dollars a day since January 2025. The region says that saves a family with a toddler and a preschooler roughly 19,372 dollars a year, though the province's goal of 10 dollars a day won't arrive until 2027. Peel runs 53,276 licensed child care spaces across 556 centres and 387 home-based sites, and children make up 42 per cent of its population, the highest share in the GTA, the plan says. The region must add 10,768 new spaces for children under six between 2024 and 2026, and about 60 per cent of those are approved, leaving just over 4,000 to go. Peel also says it needs roughly 1,245 more early years staff, and that hiring remains difficult because wages lag behind school boards.

items.title: Peel Police Respond to Person in Crisis at Mississauga Hotel Near Pearson Airport
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Peel Regional Police were called to a hotel near Toronto Pearson International Airport's Terminal 3 in Mississauga on Sunday for what officers describe as an incident involving a person in crisis. The outlet reported a large police presence remains in the area as the situation unfolds. Police said there is no threat to public safety and asked anyone nearby to follow directions from officers at the scene, according to insauga.com. Officers have not released which hotel is involved or identified the person, the outlet said. Police said more updates would be shared as they become available, insauga.com reported. The outlet listed the occurrence number as PR260387337 and noted that anyone in distress can reach Canada's 988 suicide crisis helpline, or EveryMind's 24/7 crisis line in Peel at 905-278-9036.

items.title: Mayor-Elect Tedjo Joins Ford to Open Ontario's Largest Grocery Store in Mississauga
items.summary: According to Now Toronto, Food World Plus opened to shoppers on Oct. 30 at 50 Matheson Blvd. East, becoming Ontario's largest grocery store at 176,000 square feet. The outlet reported the store centers its selling point on global food, stocking products from the Mediterranean, Latin America, Europe, Asia, Africa and the Middle East. Now Toronto said the store aims to save Mississauga's diverse population from visiting multiple specialty grocers for hard to find ingredients. Beyond groceries, the store includes a flower section, bakery, deli, fresh meat department and an in house butcher, according to the outlet. Mayor elect Alvin Tedjo attended the grand opening alongside Ontario Premier Doug Ford, Now Toronto reported. The outlet noted the meat department includes a dedicated halal section, with meat sourced from a certified halal supplier and handled according to halal standards.

items.title: Extra Daily Math and Literacy Time Lifts EQAO Scores at Toronto and Peel Schools
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, a Toronto elementary school and a Mississauga school in the Peel District School Board dramatically improved their EQAO test scores, and the newspaper drew lessons from both. The outlet detailed Corvette Junior Public School in Scarborough, where a balanced day schedule gives students 100 minutes of uninterrupted math daily, 40 more than the province requires, plus 100 minutes for literacy. The Star reported the extra math time allows for longer lessons and group work that help teachers identify struggling students. In one example, Grade 5 and 6 students worked in small groups on a word problem, writing equations and checking answers with addition. A student identified as Shaun told the Star that math is fun even when it is challenging. The newspaper said similar lessons were drawn from Mississauga's Brian W. Fleming school within the Peel board.
